bustleSliderLabel: Train position, from ceremony to reception
bustleHowAmerican: The train is lifted and hooked onto the back of the skirt, so it falls in soft poufs over the top.
bustleHowFrench: The train is tied up underneath the skirt with numbered ribbons, so it tucks under in a cascade.
bustleHowAustrian: A cord runs up the center back. Pulling it gathers the train straight up into ruched folds.
bustleHowBallroom: The train folds up underneath all the way round, so the hem sits level with the floor, like a ball gown.
bustleHowDetachable: The train is a separate piece that hooks on at the waist for the ceremony and comes off for the reception.
bustleStepAmerican1: Loops are sewn under the train.
bustleStepAmerican2: One at a time, from the center, each loop is lifted up the skirt…
bustleStepAmerican3: …and hooked onto a button at the hip.
bustleStepFrench1: Ribbons are sewn under the train.
bustleStepFrench2: From the center out, each ribbon is tucked up underneath the skirt…
bustleStepAustrian1: A cord runs through rings up the center back.
bustleStepAustrian2: Pulling the cord gathers the train upward…
bustleStepBallroom1: Ties are sewn all around the underside.
bustleStepBallroom2: The train folds under, all the way round…
bustleStepBallroom3: …so the hem sits level, like a ball gown.
bustleStepDetachable1: The train hooks on at the waist.
bustleStepDetachable3: …and the gown underneath is floor length.
